owb-dh.name: Oregon Wine Board trade site, Dundee Hills

claims.claim: The Dundee Hills AVA was approved in 2004, as Oregon's eighth AVA.
claims.note: Both give 2004. The exact day is from Wikipedia only.

claims.claim: The name started as a proposed 'Red Hills', for the red soil. The petition was amended to Dundee Hills.
Jory soil covers about 80 percent of the AVA. It is a red, well-drained volcanic clay.
claims.note: The 80 percent figure is Wikipedia only. Both agree Jory is dominant and well drained.

claims.claim: Jory formed from Columbia River basalt lava flows more than 14 million years ago. It runs 4 to 6 feet deep.
claims.quote: formed from Columbia River Basalts more than 14 million years ago
claims.note: Official wine body page. Other pages give 15 to 17 million years.

claims.claim: The steeper western slopes have Willakenzie soils, a sedimentary soil, rather than Jory.
Vineyards run from the 200 foot contour up to a high point of 1,067 feet.
claims.quote: 200-foot contour line up to a highest peak of 1,067 feet
claims.note: Both agree. Bergström's own vineyard sits at 350 to 380 feet, in the lower part of the range.

claims.claim: The Coast Range to the west puts the Dundee Hills in a rain shadow. Rain is 30 to 45 inches a year.
Nights are warmer and frost is less likely than on the valley floor. Growing seasons run a little warmer than most Willamette Valley AVAs.
claims.quote: slightly warmer than most Willamette Valley AVAs

claims.claim: Pinot Noir from Jory is often bright and elegant, with earthy, truffle-like flavors and a silky feel.
claims.quote: bright and elegant, with earthy, truffle-like flavors and a silky mouthfeel

conflicts: AVA size: Wikipedia gives 6,490 acres (infobox) and 6,940 (text). The Oregon Wine Board gives 12,500 acres. No acreage is used.
Jory age: more than 14 million years (Oregon Wine Board) against 15 to 17 million (search summaries). Neither is used as a hard figure.
gaps: TTB petition or Federal Register text not read, so the establishment date and size are not checked against the official record.
No degree-day or temperature data found.

sheet.soil: Red Jory clay, from volcanic basalt, deep and well drained.
